notes: Freshness recheck through Sep. 6 found no final Central Elections Committee merits ruling on the Damon video. Distinct CEC rulings involving other Ben-Gvir campaign videos are not transferred. summary: Central Elections Committee chair dismissed a petition seeking to prohibit free distribution of the children's book 'The Minister Who Didn't Stop.'
notes: Exculpatory/disposition record retained. The dismissal is not an adverse accountability finding and is not characterized as a broader endorsement beyond the petition's disposition. No later reversal surfaced.

summary: Fresh reporting and PMO-released chronology create a disputed timeline of Netanyahu's first hours after the Oct. 7 attack, including when he left home, reached IDF headquarters and first spoke directly with senior security chiefs.
notes: Reporting says Netanyahu was alerted by his military secretary at 06:29. The PMO says he left at 07:30 and arrived at 08:00; Shin Bet minutes reportedly put arrival at 08:22, while Channel 12 cited an unpublished office diary entry of 09:00 and another source of 09:30. PMO material says he asked at 06:44 about large-scale reserve mobilization and a strike on Hamas leadership; his first direct assessment with the IDF chief/Shin Bet chief was around 09:45-09:55. Preserve the PMO explanation that convoy preparation affected departure and that the military secretary relayed updates. No separate governance/operational-failure event is accepted without primary records and a defensible direct-responsibility finding. Netanyahu's hypothetical claim about what he would have done if awakened before the attack is not treated as directly contradicted by the post-06:29 timeline.
